text: Moat or niche comes down to where Juniper Cola's audience sits among the brands it shares taste with, and whether that position is its own.
The opening scan is already mapping Juniper Cola against five peers, so I will not repeat it. Writing the priors first, before any data comes back.
My expectation: it competes with Foxglove Cola and Harbor Seltzer, it sits near the centre of soft drinks, and its taste is fairly distinctive. A second home outside beverages would surprise me.
Resolving Foxglove Cola and Harbor Seltzer now, so step S3 can score them against Juniper Cola once the scan is back.

limitations.text: The analysis did not finish, so this note is an evidence digest assembled by code, without a full written read.
Some Qloo responses were served from an older cached copy because a fresh call failed; their fetch times show their real age.
Entities tied at a context's floor score show no measurable relationship to that signal, so they are not scored there, never ranked.
Taste signals describe audience affinity, not revenue, market share or valuation.
Peer similarity is audience taste similarity, not switching, share or sales.
A snapshot of Qloo's taste graph at fetch time; it holds no prices, filings or sales data.
Only exact name and type matches are used; close candidates are offered, never applied.
Each row comes from a single seed, and scores are compressed, so ranks are read rather than raw scores.
Entities without a score are shown as not measured.

disclaimers: Aggregated group-level taste signals; no individual-level inference.
